newsitem.title: GERMANY: Porsche says to build Boxster in Finland.
newsitem.headline: Porsche says to build Boxster in Finland.

text.p: German luxury sportscar maker Dr. Ing. h.c.F. Porsche AG said on Friday it would start producing Boxster cars at Valmet Automotive Inc. in Finland to boost output of the model in response to strong worldwide demand.
Porsche said in a statement that from the autumn of 1997 it would produce more than 5,000 cars at Valmet per year in addition to its production in Zuffenhausen, Germany.

"Scandinavia is held in high regard worldwide as a production site and Valmet has an extremely good reputation as a carmaker," Porsche said.
It added that experienced Porsche workers would be involved in production at Valmet to ensure that the cars assembled there left the plant with the "customary high Porsche quality."
Porsche added that the decision to produce Porsche cars in Finland did not affect its commitment to its German production site.
"Porsche will continue to keep capacity utilisation consistantly high in Zuffenhausen and thereby secure employment," Porsche said.
It added that the additional production in Finland would create at least 1,000 jobs at components suppliers in Germany.
Components suppliers account for four-fifths of the production of Boxster cars, and 86 percent of suppliers for the Boxster are located in Germany, Porsche said.
